correctness.rationale: For each h, PNT supplies 2h distinct odd primes d_i,e_i in fixed proportion intervals with 3/4<e_i/d_i<4/5. CRT chooses k with d_i|k and e_i|(4k+1), giving full k progression modulo P=product d_ie_i. Set n=4k, u_i=2ke_i/d_i even, v_i=d_i(4k+1)/e_i odd, and u_iv_i=n(n+1)/2. Thus endpoints (v-u+1)/2,(v+u-1)/2 are integers, interior to [1,n] by ratio bounds for sufficiently large k; their interval sum is half the total. Different ratios yield h distinct lengths <n/2 and their complementary wrapping arcs >n/2 yield 2h distinct arcs. Progression n=4k mod 4P has density 1/(4P). With primes at X=h(log h)^2, P<=(1.01X)^(2h), representative k in [P,2P), log n<=(2+o(1))h log h; hence quantitative limsup >=1. Independently checked (d,e,k)=(17,13,68): n=272, arc [127,230] length104 and its complement have target sum18564. Source code checks finite examples only; quantified proof invokes PNT/CRT.
